provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Counting 21 to 30
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count from 21 to 30
The pupils should be able to identify 20 and 30
Introduction:
We know numbers up to 20. Today we learn more numbers.
Let us count higher like we count money in the market.
Content:
Show number line from 21 to 30.
Point to each number as we count together.
Trace the number 20 with your finger in the air.
Trace the number 30 with your finger in the air.
Class activity:
Give each pupil 30 counters.
Ask them to count out 25 and put in a pile.
Evaluation questions:
Count from 21 to 30.
What number comes after 25?
Show me 30 with your fingers.
Summary:
We can count from 21 to 30.
We know 20 and 30.

topics.title: Counting 31 to 40
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count from 31 to 40
The pupils should be able to locate 35 on a number line
Introduction:
We counted up to 30 last week. Now we count more.
Think of 35 naira for buying plantain chips.
Content:
Count from 31 to 40 slowly.
Point to each number on the big number line.
Find 35 on the number line.
Circle 35 with your finger.
Class activity:
Give pupils number cards 31 to 40.
Call out a number and pupils hold up the card.
Evaluation questions:
Count from 31 to 40.
What number comes before 38?
Point to 35 on the number line.
Summary:
We can count from 31 to 40.
We found 35 on the number line.

topics.title: Counting 41 to 50
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count from 41 to 50
The pupils should be able to trace the number 50
Introduction:
We learned numbers up to 40. Now we go to 50.
Think of 50 naira for buying groundnut.
Content:
Count from 41 to 50 together.
Show the number 50 on the board.
Trace 50 with your finger in the air.
Trace 50 in your exercise book.
Class activity:
Give pupils sand trays to write 50.
They trace the number 50 with their fingers.
Evaluation questions:
Count from 41 to 50.
What number comes after 45?
Trace the number 50 in the air.
Summary:
We can count from 41 to 50.
We traced the number 50.

topics.title: Counting 1 to 50
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count from 1 to 50
The pupils should be able to fill in missing numbers
Introduction:
We learned numbers 1 to 30, 31 to 40 and 41 to 50.
Now we count all together like we count our toys.
Content:
Count from 1 to 50 in parts.
Stop at 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50.
Fill in missing numbers on the board.
Example: 5, _, 7, 25, _, 27.
Class activity:
Write numbers 1 to 50 with gaps on the board.
Pupils fill in the missing numbers.
Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 50.
What number is missing? 10, _, 12.
Fill in 35, _, 37.
Summary:
We counted from 1 to 50.
We filled missing numbers correctly.

topics.title: Simple addition with objects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add two groups of objects
The pupils should be able to count the total
Introduction:
We know how to count. Today we add things together.
Like when you add two yam tubers and one more.
Content:
Put two blocks on the table.
Add one more block.
Count all blocks together.
2 + 1 = 3 blocks.
Class activity:
Give pupils small objects like counters.
Put two objects in one hand and one in the other.
Count all objects together.
Evaluation questions:
If you have 2 pencils and add 1, how many?
Put 3 beans and add 2 beans. Count all.
What is 2 + 1?
Summary:
We can add two groups of objects.
We count the total correctly.

topics.title: Simple subtraction with objects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to take away objects
The pupils should be able to count what is left
Introduction:
We know how to add. Today we take away.
Like when you eat some of your sweets.
Content:
Put five sweets on the table.
Eat one sweet.
Count how many sweets are left.
5 - 1 = 4 sweets.
Class activity:
Give pupils five counters each.
Ask them to take away one counter.
Count how many are left.
Evaluation questions:
If you have 4 mangoes and eat one, how many left?
Take away 2 from 5. What is left?
What is 5 - 1?
Summary:
We can take away objects.
We count what is left correctly.

topics.title: Shapes around us
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify circle, square and triangle
The pupils should be able to find circles in the classroom
Introduction:
We see shapes every day. Today we learn about them.
Like the round clock and square window in our class.
Content:
Show a circle. It is round with no corners.
Show a square. It has four equal sides.
Show a triangle. It has three sides.
Find circles in the classroom.
Class activity:
Go on a shape hunt in the classroom.
Pupils point to circles, squares and triangles.
Evaluation questions:
What shape is like a wheel?
What shape has three sides?
Find a circle in our classroom.
Summary:
We know circle, square and triangle.
We found circles in our class.

topics.title: Sorting by size and colour
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sort objects by colour
The pupils should be able to sort objects by size
Introduction:
We can sort things like in the market.
Group things that are the same together.
Content:
Put all red blocks together.
Put all blue blocks together.
Put all big books together.
Put all small books together.
Class activity:
Give pupils mixed blocks of different colours and sizes.
Ask them to sort by colour then by size.
Evaluation questions:
Sort all red objects together.
Sort all big objects together.
How many blue blocks do you have?
Summary:
We can sort by colour and size.
We grouped same things together.

topics.title: Patterns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to copy a simple colour pattern
The pupils should be able to continue a pattern
Introduction:
We see patterns in clothes and on walls.
Patterns repeat in a special way.
Content:
Show a colour pattern: red, blue, red, blue.
Pupils copy the pattern with coloured blocks.
Continue the pattern: red, blue, red, what next?
Class activity:
Make a pattern with objects on the table.
Pupils continue the pattern.
Evaluation questions:
Copy this pattern: red, blue, red.
What comes next in red, blue, red, blue?
Make your own pattern with blocks.
Summary:
We can copy and continue patterns.
Patterns repeat in order.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count from 1 to 50
The pupils should be able to add and subtract with objects
The pupils should be able to find shapes in the classroom
Introduction:
Today we practice all we learned this term.
Let us count, add, subtract and find shapes.
Content:
Count from 1 to 50 in turns.
Add two groups of objects.
Take away objects and count what is left.
Find circles, squares and triangles in class.
Class activity:
Shape hunt in the classroom.
Count objects and add or subtract.
Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 50.
Add 2 and 3.
Take away 1 from 4.
Find a triangle in our classroom.
Summary:
We practiced counting, adding and subtracting.
We found shapes in our class.
